title: "GIC Lab"
subtitle: "Open, controlled research on learned agent architecture"

::: {.callout-note}
## Phase 0 only

No prototype, benchmark, training run, or paid GPU job has been executed. The current artifact is the research control plane: hypotheses, provenance, experiment contracts, validation, and publication infrastructure.
:::

GIC Lab studies a narrower and more falsifiable question than “can we build a GIC agent?”:

> Which proposed mechanisms are necessary, sufficient, learnable, and measurably better than matched external orchestration?

The program begins with the authors' released SiRA and SR²AM references, then isolates one mechanism at a time under declared resource budgets. Negative and inconclusive evidence is a valid outcome.

## Current work

- Pin primary papers, repositories, and released model revisions.
- Separate source claims from project interpretations.
- Define typed lifecycle, evidence, outcome, transition, artifact, and compute contracts.
- Build a public notebook that cannot silently turn placeholders into results.
- Prepare an independent human/agent reading reconciliation before Phase 1.

See [project status](generated/status.qmd), the [claim map](research/claims.qmd), and the generated [experiment registry](generated/experiments.qmd).
